materials.title: Structural Analysis and Statics
materials.summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Structural Analysis and Statics.
notes: Equilibrium and reactions

Isolate the structure, identify support constraints and all external actions, then apply force and moment equilibrium. Symmetry may simplify reactions, but only after the load and support geometry are verified.
Beams and diagrams
Distributed loads reduce to resultants for reactions; shear is the derivative of moment, so a smooth interior moment extremum occurs where shear is zero. Preserve sign conventions consistently.
Trusses and resultants
At ideal pin joints, resolve member forces along member axes. Zero-force rules require the stated joint loading and connectivity; they are not visual guesses.
Stability and deformation
Euler buckling is an ideal elastic model sensitive to effective length. Deflection formulas require their stated load, support, small-deformation, and prismatic-member assumptions.

materials.title: Strength and Mechanics of Materials
materials.summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Strength and Mechanics of Materials.
notes: Stress, strain, and stiffness
Average normal stress is axial force divided by area; elastic strain is stress divided by modulus and elongation is strain times original length. Keep force and area units compatible.
Section response
The centroidal second moment for a rectangle is bd cubed over 12 about the axis parallel to b. Elastic bending stress equals moment divided by section modulus at the extreme fiber.
Combined and local effects

A hole reduces net area and can raise local elastic stress through a stated concentration factor. Offset loads add moments; fatigue models combine mean and alternating stress only under their declared assumptions.
Material interpretation
Concrete cylinder strength is failure load divided by specimen area. Ductility, stiffness, fatigue resistance, and strength describe different behaviors and should not be substituted for one another.

materials.title: Applied Mathematics for Civil Engineering
materials.summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Applied Mathematics for Civil Engineering.
notes: Model setup
Translate geometry, rates, percentages, and unit scales into one consistent system before calculating. Check dimensions and estimate the expected magnitude.
Optimization and calculus
Differentiate a continuous response to locate candidate extrema, then check the allowed interval and endpoints. Integrate rates over the stated interval to obtain accumulated quantities.
Ratios and scaling
Map scale, grade, productivity, density, and utilization are ratios with different denominators. Write the numerator and denominator labels before inserting values.
Data interpretation
Use tables and trends as evidence within their measured range. A departure from linearity, uncertainty interval, or limiting constraint must be interpreted rather than merely copied.

materials.title: Surveying, Leveling, and Layout
materials.summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Surveying, Leveling, and Layout.
notes: Scale and direction
Convert map length using the representative fraction and compatible units. Distinguish azimuth from an interior or deflection angle before applying a turn.
Leveling

Height of instrument equals known elevation plus backsight; the next elevation equals height of instrument minus foresight. Arithmetic closure checks observations but does not identify every field blunder.
Traverse components
Resolve each line into latitude and departure with consistent signs; algebraic sums show closure error or net displacement, depending on whether the traverse is intended to close.
Field control
Protect benchmarks, record observations in sequence, repeat critical checks, and connect layout to a documented datum rather than an assumed local reference.

materials.title: Transportation and Highway Engineering
materials.summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Transportation and Highway Engineering.
notes: Traffic stream variables
Flow, speed, and density satisfy q=kv under a consistent macroscopic model. Average values and observation intervals must refer to the same traffic stream.
Signals and capacity
An idealized approach capacity can be estimated from saturation flow times effective-green ratio; compare demand with that capacity before inferring oversaturation.
Horizontal alignment
For a simple circular curve, tangent length is R tan(delta/2) with delta in the angle convention expected by the calculation.
Grades and profiles
Percent grade is rise over horizontal run times 100. A change from positive to negative grade forms a crest profile; the reverse forms a sag profile.

materials.title: Construction Quantities and Productivity
materials.summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Construction Quantities and Productivity.
notes: Quantity takeoff
Compute geometric quantities in consistent dimensions, then apply material rates. Separate direct quantity changes from overhead, profit, waste, and contractual adjustments unless supplied.
Productivity
Productivity is output divided by the relevant labor, equipment, or elapsed-time input. Compare crews on the same basis and include utilization when converting theoretical to effective capacity.
Method control
A workable method statement connects sequence, resources, interfaces, hazards, quality checks, and acceptance responsibilities; a schedule alone does not control execution risk.
Records and change
Document measured quantities, assumptions, approvals, and affected work. A unit-price quantity change uses the supported incremental quantity before other contract effects are considered.

materials.title: Fluid Mechanics, Pipe Flow, and Open Channels
materials.summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Fluid Mechanics, Pipe Flow, and Open Channels.
notes: Hydrostatics
Pressure head and pressure use p=gamma h; resultant hydrostatic force on a plane area uses pressure at its centroid. Buoyancy equals displaced-fluid weight.
Continuity and energy
For incompressible steady flow, discharge equals area times mean velocity. Total head combines elevation, pressure, and velocity heads, while losses reduce available head along real systems.
Pumps
Hydraulic power is rho g Q H; required shaft power divides hydraulic power by efficiency. Cavitation assessment requires suction-side pressure and vapor-pressure context.
Open channels
Hydraulic radius is area divided by wetted perimeter. Froude number and specific energy distinguish subcritical, critical, and supercritical states under the stated section assumptions.

materials.title: Soil Properties, Effective Stress, and Seepage
materials.summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Soil Properties, Effective Stress, and Seepage.
notes: Phase relationships
Water content is water mass over dry-soil mass; void ratio is void volume over solid volume. Unit weight, density, porosity, and void ratio are related but not interchangeable.
Classification and compaction

Grain-size measures and Atterberg limits support standardized classification. A compaction curve identifies maximum dry unit weight and its corresponding optimum water content for the specified effort.
Effective stress and strength
Effective stress is total stress minus pore pressure. Mohr–Coulomb strength combines cohesion and effective-normal-stress friction under the stated drained or undrained model.
Seepage
Darcy discharge is permeability times hydraulic gradient times area. Exit gradients near or above critical values indicate piping or heave concern, not a guaranteed failure time.

materials.title: Foundations, Settlement, and Stability
materials.summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Foundations, Settlement, and Stability.
notes: Bearing and contact pressure
Average footing pressure is service load divided by plan area. Allowable-capacity comparisons must keep service and ultimate bases distinct and use the stated safety factor.
Settlement
Consolidation settlement follows compressibility, layer thickness, stress history, drainage, and time. A void-ratio relation is valid only with the defined initial condition and strain convention.
Slopes and retaining systems

Factor of safety compares available resistance with driving actions on the assumed mechanism. Water pressure and seepage alter both loading and effective stress, so drainage can be structurally significant.
Failure interpretation

General shear commonly shows a defined failure surface and ground heave; punching is more localized. Rapid loading of saturated clay is often assessed with an undrained model when drainage cannot occur.

materials.title: Civil Engineering Data and Laboratory Interpretation
materials.summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Civil Engineering Data and Laboratory Interpretation.
notes: Tables and trends
Identify controlled and measured variables, units, and the comparison basis before selecting a trend. Do not infer causation or extrapolate beyond the supplied data without support.
Laboratory response
Initial linearity can establish a reference slope; departure, scatter, and outliers require checking calibration, specimen behavior, and repeatability before assigning a mechanism.
Derived parameters
Compute ratios such as permeability comparisons, strength slopes, or intercepts from consistent test conditions. A larger input does not imply a larger response when another governing factor changes.
Reporting
Retain significant figures appropriate to the data, state assumptions, and distinguish observed results from model-based interpretation.

materials.title: Construction Safety, Materials, and Quality
materials.summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Construction Safety, Materials, and Quality.
notes: Quality control and assurance
Field tests verify that placed work meets the project basis; they supplement process control rather than substitute for documented requirements and representative sampling.
Concrete and durability

Curing preserves moisture and temperature conditions needed for hydration. Marine chloride exposure calls for a coherent durability strategy addressing permeability, cover, cracking, materials, and detailing without inventing a universal limit.
Execution safety

Method review should identify sequence, temporary conditions, interfaces, hazards, controls, hold points, and responsibilities. Compliance values come from the governing project and jurisdiction, not generic study notes.
Evidence and decisions
Investigate nonconforming or unusual results before assigning cause. Use calibrated tests, traceable records, and acceptance criteria appropriate to the work.

materials.title: Hydrology, Water Supply, and Drainage
materials.summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Hydrology, Water Supply, and Drainage.
notes: Demand and storage
Convert per-capita demand and population to daily volume, then apply explicitly stated losses and balancing duration. Keep demand, production, and storage periods distinct.
Runoff estimation
The rational method combines runoff coefficient, rainfall intensity, and drainage area with a unit-conversion constant; it assumes the supplied intensity and catchment representation are appropriate.
Hydrographs
Runoff volume over an interval is area under discharge above the selected baseflow. With equal intervals, compare average excess ordinates rather than one peak alone.
Drainage reasoning
Drainage systems manage collection, conveyance, storage, and safe discharge. Capacity conclusions require the relevant storm, boundary conditions, losses, and downstream controls.

materials.title: Structural Testing and Nondestructive Evaluation
materials.summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Structural Testing and Nondestructive Evaluation.
notes: Test planning
Define the property, expected response, load range, instrumentation, and acceptance basis before testing. Calibration and repeatability are prerequisites to interpreting small differences.
Response interpretation
Compare measured response with the initial trend and an appropriate model; nonlinearity can indicate several mechanisms and should not be assigned a cause without corroboration.
Nondestructive methods
Liquid penetrant reveals surface-breaking discontinuities in suitable nonporous materials; other methods are selected for subsurface, volumetric, or material-specific targets.
Limits of evidence
An indication is not automatically a defect, and a nondetection is not proof of absence. Method sensitivity, access, geometry, preparation, and operator procedure bound conclusions.

materials.title: Engineering Economics and Project Scheduling
materials.summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Engineering Economics and Project Scheduling.
notes: Economic equivalence
Compare cash flows at a common time using the stated interest rate and timing convention. NPV subtracts the initial investment from discounted benefits and costs.
Cost models

Straight-line depreciation spreads depreciable basis over service life; equivalent annual cost converts alternatives to a common annual basis. These models do not replace technical feasibility checks.
Network scheduling
A finish-to-start network duration follows the longest controlling path. Recalculate path floats after duration or logic changes rather than assuming the original critical path remains controlling.
Decision records
State analysis period, price basis, included costs, assumptions, and uncertainty. Nominal undiscounted totals and present worth answer different questions.

materials.title: Reinforced Concrete, Steel, and Connections
materials.summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Reinforced Concrete, Steel, and Connections.
notes: Reinforced-concrete behavior

Concrete is strong in compression but weak in tension, so longitudinal reinforcement crosses tensile regions and develops force through bond. Reinforcement ratio uses steel area divided by the stated concrete reference area.
Members and limit states
Beam, column, and connection behavior depends on load path and failure mode. Keep service demand, factored demand, nominal capacity, and any explicitly supplied reduction separate.
Steel members and connections

Gross yielding, net-section behavior, shear, tension, weld throat, eccentricity, and resultant actions are distinct checks. Use only the resistance expression and factors supplied or authoritatively specified.
Ductility and seismic response
Repeated reversals favor stable inelastic deformation and energy dissipation. Ductility does not mean unlimited deformation or remove the need for strength and detailing checks.
Code-currentness practice

Use the current applicable authority for version-sensitive requirements. Record the edition or retrieval date, distinguish a stable load-path principle from a project-specific code limit, and do not turn an undated remembered section number into a universal answer.
Design-basis review
Before using a supplied factor or limit, identify the action, limit state, material, jurisdiction, and stated code basis. Escalate a genuine conflict rather than silently averaging requirements.

materials.title: Prestressed Concrete Foundations for CELE Review
materials.summary: Source-first Civil Engineering study foundation for basic prestressing principles, construction sequence, stress resultants, losses, and service behavior within current CELE scope.
notes: Purpose and scope

Prestressing introduces a controlled compression pattern to offset part of the tensile response from service actions. The CELE-level treatment is conceptual and application-oriented; it does not assume specialist bridge detailing.
Pretensioning and post-tensioning

Pretensioned tendons are stressed before concrete placement and transfer occurs after the concrete reaches the required condition. Post-tensioned tendons are stressed after concrete placement and use anchorages and the specified duct or tendon system.
Section stress behavior

For a simple average stress check, prestressing force is divided by the relevant area. An eccentric force also creates a force-couple moment. Sign convention and tendon location must be stated before interpreting compression or tension at a fiber.
Loss mechanisms

Elastic shortening, creep, shrinkage, steel relaxation, anchorage seating, and friction or wobble effects where applicable can reduce effective prestress. A question must identify which losses are supplied and avoid double counting.
Service implications
Prestressing can reduce service tensile stress and cracking tendency, but service stress, deflection, durability, anchorage, and construction-stage behavior still require separate checks.
Common errors
Do not treat initial jacking force as effective service force, confuse pretensioning with post-tensioning, or claim that prestressing guarantees zero cracking or deflection.

materials.title: Governing Structural Codes and Currentness for CELE Review
materials.summary: Study foundation for distinguishing the current CELE scope authority, stable engineering principles, version-sensitive requirements, and defensible code-based application.
notes: Authority hierarchy

The current PRC CELE program establishes examination scope. A recognized project code, regulation, or official authority controls a version-sensitive design requirement; instructional notes explain principles but do not replace that authority.
Stable principle versus requirement

Equilibrium, load path, strength behavior, and serviceability concepts can be taught as stable principles. Numerical limits, factors, editions, and jurisdiction-specific requirements must be tied to the current controlling source.
Application reading
Interpret a code-based question by identifying the member, action, limit state, material, jurisdiction, edition, and supplied factors before selecting an answer.
Documentation
A defensible engineering decision records the controlling source and version or retrieval date, states assumptions, and distinguishes an official requirement from a study simplification.
Common errors
Avoid undated section-number trivia, silently averaging conflicting requirements, treating a textbook shortcut as a code rule, or using a value outside its stated scope.
